title: Use a correlogram only to scan many variables for experts.
rule: Use a correlogram, a reference form, to show the correlation between every pair of a set of variables as a grid: each cell shaded on a diverging scale from negative to positive, with the coefficient printed in it. Order the variables so related ones sit together, and say which coefficient the cells hold.
use_when: A specialist asks which of many measures move together before choosing pairs to study.

use_instead.when: A few variables, each pair worth seeing as points

text: A grid of coefficients puts dozens of pairs in one view, but a coefficient hides the shape of each relationship. It suits a first scan by experts, before the pairs that matter get charts of their own.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: No kit form: draw a correlogram with diverging pair B and the coefficient printed in each cell.
sketch_alt: A five-by-five grid of squares, each shaded on a diverging scale by the correlation between two variables, dark at the strongest pairs and pale near zero.
